A successful call means both gates passed: the type belongs to the supported family, and the particular sum is representable.

topics.summary: Traits describe type properties, if constexpr selects implementations, and concepts constrain interfaces. None of them replaces runtime representability checks or semantic laws. A robust generic function states what the compiler can check, what the caller must guarantee, and what the function validates while executing. Clear boundaries make diagnostics shorter and correctness arguments stronger.
